newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mostly higher.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended mostly higher on Wednesday, after technical buying by individual investors supported the market, traders said.
Prices were 10 yen lower to 180 yen higher. The benchmark September 1997 contract was up 60 yen at 16,060 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 71,426 lots.

The weaker Chicago corn market overnight triggered selling by local investors in early morning, the traders said. But price gains in CBOT overnight corn trading encouraged investors to buy later. "Investors hold many longs and are quick to liquidate them when prices gain," a trader said.
Benchmark September is likely to fall to the 15,000 yen level when investors start liquidating long positions, the traders said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.10-1/2 per bushel at 0825 GMT, unchanged from Tuesday's close.
The spot November of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.90-1/2 at 0825 GMT, against $7.91-1/4 price at Tuesday's close.
